grh_ba40f28feeb1cb51dae9.title: The Adventure of the Blarney Stone
paragraphs: After abrasive Jeffrey Hankin bets that he will kiss the Blarney Stone, partner Michael Corcoran lowers him headfirst over the castle wall and apparently loses his grip when Hankin's boots prove greased. Holmes rejects suspicion against the hotel boot cleaner and reconstructs the climb. Corcoran's love for Hankin's wife supplies the motive, while his failure to react naturally to the grease betrays the method: he smeared the boots only as he took hold of them, making the murder look like someone else's earlier sabotage. Holmes proposes checking for the absence of road dust in the grease; exposed, Corcoran leaps from the parapet to his death.

This [[show|the-new-adventures-of-sherlock-holmes|The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes]] broadcast aired on March 18, 1946. [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer, Anthony Boucher as writer, Denis Green as writer, and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.482f355195f87565|A Case of Identity]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_ba9842ba27dd49e36b71.title: Powder River Policy
paragraphs: A worn former soldier finds a badly wounded preacher beside an overturned wagon and brings him into a Wyoming town whose residents are more interested in betting on whether the stranger will live than in helping him. Drawing on hard-earned battlefield experience, the old soldier takes control, removes the bullet and refuses to accept the common belief that the preacher is doomed. He learns that the wounded man was carrying money to build a church and was traveling to marry a woman already waiting in town, then brings her to his bedside to give him another reason to fight. When the preacher revives enough to speak, the old soldier also recognizes that the weapon carried by Dokes matches the kind that fired the bullet and helps expose the shooting. His unexpected competence earns him a place and steady work in the town.
This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on March 12, 1979. It is listed as episode 26 in the archive.
